metadata.title: Metric formula lab
metadata.subtitle: Every metric needs a formula, unit, window, owner, and decision use.

items.decision: Use revenue to size the business, then pair it with margin before recommending action.
items.example_context: Q1 chain-wide net revenue after refunds and discounts.
items.caution: Gross sales and net revenue answer different questions.

items.decision: Use AOV to separate growth from larger baskets versus growth from more transactions.
items.example_context: Average completed Bean & Basket order in March.
items.caution: Large catering orders can pull the mean upward.

items.decision: Use margin rate to keep revenue growth from hiding discounting or cost pressure.
items.example_context: March beverage margin after milk, beans, pastry, and packaging costs.
items.caution: Cost allocation rules change the answer.

items.decision: Use conversion to distinguish demand problems from execution problems.
items.example_context: App visitors who completed an order after seeing a featured drink.
items.caution: Bots, staff tests, and repeat refreshes are not demand.

items.numerator: customers crossing churn rule this month
items.denominator: customers active at start of month
items.window: Monthly, with a written churn rule
items.decision: Use churn to monitor retention health and trigger a deeper causal question about what changed.
items.example_context: Customers with no purchase for 60 days, among those active on March 1.
items.caution: A different inactivity window creates a different churn rate.

items.decision: Use repeat purchase to judge whether acquisition is creating durable demand.
items.example_context: January first-time customers who returned within 60 days.
items.caution: Lifetime repeat rates favor older cohorts.

items.decision: Use ARPU to compare customer value across markets with different customer counts.
items.example_context: March net revenue divided by customers with at least one March purchase.
items.caution: The active-customer rule determines the denominator.

items.decision: Use share when the decision is competitive position, not internal growth alone.
items.example_context: Packaged beans share in the downtown specialty coffee category.
